implementation_status: Source implements Eleanor recruitment and cattle activity, the full Lanterns at the Ford crossing, Ada steam repair and the full Two Seats, One Regulator cart outing, Ines's three-clue spirit trail and camp/field assignment, separate romance choices, camp recovery, and saved character state. Detailed character animation and room visual acceptance remain unfinished.

decisions.decision: Harem-lit alternate 1870s Weird West with steam robotics/mechas, ordinary accepted spirits and ambiguous occult gods battling on Earth, built on top of a real period-economics and cattle-ranching simulation (see 'simulation_pillars' below). 'Supersedes a purely historical cattle-drive identity' from the original version of this decision meant the Weird West elements are real and load-bearing, not that ranching/economics stopped being the game's core -- the two are not in tension.
decisions.consequence: Neither half is decorative. A companion's usefulness, a rival outfit's pressure and a trade good's price are the same simulation as the ghosts and the machines, not a separate skin over it.

decisions.decision: Dan, 2026-09-10: think of the whole project first as a simulation of period economics and cattle ranching specifically, not a companion-collector with a ranch skin. The player grows through four connected levers: shrewd dealing (trade, negotiation, debt, market timing), successful cattle drives (herding, trail risk, delivery), exploration (the wider county and beyond, not one fixed room), and romance (harem-lit, unchanged). This is a reframing of priority and design lens, not a reversal of the existing scope decision below -- design work on economy and exploration can and should proceed now; committing new systems to the actual Godot room still waits for the same room-at-a-time discipline everything else has followed.
decisions.consequence: New design work (design/ECONOMY.md, design/EXPLORATION.md) treats trade, market pricing, debt and county travel as first-class systems on the same footing as companions and madness, not optional later content. Existing trade/craft characters (Nettie Voss, Consuelo Diaz, the Widow Stroud, Cyrus Boone, Georgiana Hollis, Adelheid Kraus, and others already in design/npcs.json and design/characters.json) are the economy's actors, not flavor -- design/ECONOMY.md is written to reuse them rather than invent a parallel merchant roster.

decisions.decision: All romance women are adults 18 or older, mostly 18–24; older adults allowed. Slim, small-busted adult silhouettes and provocative PG-13 clothing.
decisions.consequence: Explicit age in all authored/generated romance records; no child-coded design. Earlier proposed 21+ minimum is superseded.

decisions.decision: Eligible women are recruitable harem companions, including named and procedural characters with individual perks.
decisions.consequence: Model stable identity, recruitment and perks independently of relationship stage.

decisions.decision: Everyone has madness; intimacy with loved ones reduces it.
decisions.consequence: Shared madness contract covers player, companions, rustlers and other NPCs.

decisions.decision: Voluntary adult relationships; PG-13 affection and fade-to-black intimacy; shared rest and support count as intimacy.
decisions.consequence: No mandatory sexual transaction for recruitment or recovery.
Replace the prior 1868 HUD date; this is an alternate-history starting-date choice.

decisions.decision: Eleanor is age 24 and a frontier healer familiar with spirits.
decisions.consequence: Preserve existing room sprite; do not claim new outfit approval.

decisions.decision: Prove the current single room before broadening scope; repair lasso and animation sequence quality.
decisions.consequence: Future relationship, madness and supernatural systems remain design only until the room visual bar is met.

decisions.decision: Madness 0–100, four bands, sample perks, recovery amount/time/caps and relationship stage names.
decisions.consequence: Untested values require a bounded implementation and playtest.

decisions.decision: Dan, 2026-09-10: the romance roster should be large -- hundreds of options over time -- and the wider named/minor cast should run into many hundreds, each with a distinct reason for being, story, lore and quests. This resolves the roster-limit half of the old 'unresolved' entry below.
decisions.consequence: This is reached two ways, not by hand-authoring hundreds of full companion.schema.json records in one sitting (that would either take an enormous amount of sustained work or degrade into repetitive filler, neither of which serves 'each unique'): (1) the procedural generator (scripts/character_factory.gd, design/characters.json's procedural_template) now draws from much larger name/temperament pools and seven distinct family archetypes with their own hooks and perks, so every generated companion the system can produce is genuinely differentiated, not just renamed; (2) hand-authored named companions (full romance mechanics, unique quests) and minor/supporting characters (design/npcs.json's lighter schema) continue in large organized batches session over session. The real ceiling today is art, not writing: the procedural generator can only place a visible companion for one of the 96 extracted candidates in kits/character-families/catalog.json, none of which are 'approved' status yet -- see design/CHARACTER-VISUAL-CONTRACT.md and the art-admission process already established in VALIDATION.md/VISUAL-AUDIT.md. Written/lore-level characters are not blocked by that ceiling and can scale ahead of it.

decisions.decision: Death/departure persistence policy, world scale, machine economy, mecha control and exact procedural background weights.
decisions.consequence: Do not silently implement assumptions as accepted design.

decisions.decision: Ordinary but gorgeous adult women who are slim, small-chested, healthy, active, charming and self-confident; self-chosen rebellious PG-13 clothing is secondary to personality.
decisions.consequence: Supersedes a cast organized around revealing fantasy outfits alone.

decisions.decision: Most romance develops through gameplay, playing as companions and short unique RPG adventures, with mutual attraction and short lively dialogue.
decisions.consequence: Avoid endless conversation trees, begging and constant refusal/persuasion loops; each companion gets a distinct playable adventure beat.

decisions.decision: Switch control for a bounded authored adventure while preserving actor identity and state, then return safely with rewards applied once.
decisions.consequence: The source switches control for Eleanor cattle/lantern activities and Ada cart driving, with persisted checkpoints and return control.

decisions.decision: Build out the game following the design while walk and turn work continues, including generated tweens and parallel agents.
decisions.consequence: Supersedes the earlier implementation freeze pending full room visual approval; visual acceptance remains unproven.

decisions.decision: Reject the coarse Ada walk sheet; produce richly detailed adult masters and daring PG-13 wardrobe variants with visible skin and confident self-expression.
decisions.consequence: design/CHARACTER-VISUAL-CONTRACT.md supersedes the 40-pixel production target. Native crops and 160-pixel figure candidates are retained. The renderer supports display density and source-pixel metadata; these candidates are not live room replacements.

decisions.decision: The four Ines summer outfits establish the general adult-cast clothing level: non-nude, daring, intended for a teen audience.
decisions.consequence: Use this coverage and styling in future wardrobe prompts; camera, motion and runtime admission remain separate.

decisions.decision: Use Lara Croft as a reference for adult athletic adventure appeal, while retaining the 1870s period. Skirts are welcome; the cast need not wear modern shorts and halters.
decisions.consequence: Daring coverage comes from period fabrics, fitted vests and bodices, tied blouses, short or split riding skirts, leather and brass. Weird West permits inventive tailoring without defaulting to contemporary clothing.
